title: Talking about past experiences
objectives: Say what you have done in your life without giving a date
Ask a classmate about their experiences
Tell the difference between an experience (present perfect) and a finished event (past simple)

keywords.definition: at any time in your life (used in questions)
at no time in your life
keywords.example: She has never seen the sea.
I have already finished my homework.

keywords.definition: until now (used in questions and negative sentences)
keywords.example: I haven't called my sister yet.
Riding a boat on the river was a great experience.

grammar.title: Present perfect: form
grammar.rule: Use have/has + past participle. Use it to talk about experiences in your life, when the exact time is not important or not given.

forms.affirmative: I/you/we/they have + past participle; he/she/it has + past participle
forms.negative: have not (haven't) / has not (hasn't) + past participle
forms.question: Have/Has + subject + past participle?

examples.note: After have/has we need the past participle.

examples.correct: Has she ever travelled by plane?
examples.incorrect: Does she ever travelled by plane?
examples.note: Do not use do/does with the present perfect.

commonMistakes: Using the infinitive instead of the past participle (I have go)
frenchSpeakerTraps: In French the passé composé is also used for finished past events; in English we use the past simple for those.

grammar.title: Present perfect or past simple?
grammar.rule: If we say or ask WHEN (yesterday, last year, in 2019, two days ago), use the past simple. If the time is not given and the experience matters now, use the present perfect.

examples.correct: I have been to Brazzaville. I went there last year.
examples.incorrect: I have been to Brazzaville last year.
examples.note: last year = finished time, so past simple (went).

commonMistakes: Using the present perfect with a finished time (I have seen him yesterday)
frenchSpeakerTraps: « J'ai vu ce film hier » = I saw this film yesterday (not: I have seen).

functionalPhrases: I've already ... but I haven't ... yet.

speakingTasks.prompt: Tell me about something interesting you have done in your life.
You meet a new classmate. Ask three questions about places they have visited or food they have tried.
Say one thing you have already done today and one thing you haven't done yet. Then tell me about one thing you did yesterday.

tutorNotes: Students are French speakers. Be gentle with participles of irregular verbs: it is the most common difficulty. Keep scenarios imaginary or about everyday life, never ask for private details.
